findings.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-17 — should_block? does a read-modify-write (match_count += 1 then save) with no locking/retry; concurrent signups can lose match-count increments
[Medium/concurrency] app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-17 — record.save's return value is ignored, so failed writes silently drop stats

[Medium/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:19-21 — domain regex @(#{domains}) is not anchored, matching blocked/whitelisted domains as substrings anywhere in the address (e.g. user@gmail.com.evil.com matches gmail.com); should anchor to end of string or parse the actual domain part

[Medium/bug] app/models/blocked_email.rb:9 / user.rb — email lookups and uniqueness checks are case-sensitive, so blocking bad@spam.com does not block BAD@SPAM.COM and uniqueness permits duplicates differing only by case; use case-insensitive lookup and unique index

[Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:68-73 — client-side check reports rejected emails with generic user.email.invalid message instead of surfacing the server's specific block reason

[Medium/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb — the new EmailValidator never validates email format; it appears to rely on a separate format validator gem/config not added in this diff, so format validation may silently no-op

[Low/security] app/controllers/users_controller.rb:197-199 — returning errors and values (including the submitted email) in the JSON response enables enumeration of blocklisted email addresses; consider a generic error for blocked emails

[Low/performance] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:11 — BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a DB write (counter update) during model validation on every signup attempt, adding write load and taking a row lock in the request path; consider debouncing or async stats updates

[Medium/test_gap] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb — tests only stub should_block?; no tests for whitelist/blacklist regex paths (including substring-matching edge case) and no spec for the new errors/values JSON payload in UsersController#create

[Low/bug] app/models/blocked_email.rb:23 — self.action_type ||= BlockedEmail.actions[:block] relies on Enum not starting at 0; if :block maps to 0, ||= treats the explicitly-set value as unset (fragile if the enum changes)
[Low/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb — file is missing a trailing newline, which can cause patch/tooling churn

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-17 — record.save's return value is ignored, so failed writes silently drop stats

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (new `app/models/blocked_email.rb`), when a matching record is found it mutates `match_count` and `last_match_at` and then calls `record.save` without checking the boolean return or handling failures. If the write fails (e.g., DB error, unexpected validation failure), the method will still return the block decision (`record && record.action_type == ...`) and the stats update will be silently lost. This doesn’t break blocking behavior, but it is a real, diff-grounded robustness/observability issue for the new stats-tracking feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:19-21 — domain regex @(#{domains}) is not anchored, matching blocked/whitelisted domains as substrings anywhere in the address (e.g. user@gmail.com.evil.com matches gmail.com); should anchor to end of string or parse the actual domain part

adjudication.rationale: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb, email_in_restriction_setting? builds `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` and checks `value =~ regexp`. This is not anchored to the end of the string or limited to the actual domain portion, so an email like `user@gmail.com.evil.com` would match `@gmail.com` and be incorrectly treated as whitelisted/blacklisted. The diff introduces this validator and continues using this regex for domain restriction checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:68-73 — client-side check reports rejected emails with generic user.email.invalid message instead of surfacing the server's specific block reason

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a client-side cache `rejectedEmails` and, if the current email is in that list, `emailValidation` returns `failed: true` with `reason: I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` (create_account_controller.js). However, the server can now reject emails with more specific messages (e.g., `user.email.blocked` via the new `EmailValidator`, or `user.email.not_allowed`). The client only stores the rejected email address (`pushObject(result.values.email)`) and discards the specific server-side error, so subsequent validations will show the generic `user.email.invalid` instead of the specific reason. This is a UX/clarity issue rather than a correctness break, since the email is still rejected either way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb — the new EmailValidator never validates email format; it appears to rely on a separate format validator gem/config not added in this diff, so format validation may silently no-op

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `validates :email, email: true` in `user.rb` clearly invokes the newly added `EmailValidator` (Rails convention), and that validator does run logic (domain whitelist/blacklist plus `BlockedEmail.should_block?`). So it’s not “silently no-op” due to missing gem/config. Also, the previous `email_validator` method that was removed did not validate email *format* either—only domain restrictions—so the finding’s premise about format validation being expected/removed is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] app/controllers/users_controller.rb:197-199 — returning errors and values (including the submitted email) in the JSON response enables enumeration of blocklisted email addresses; consider a generic error for blocked emails

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name","username","email")` to the unauthenticated `UsersController#create` failure JSON, which makes it easier for a client to programmatically distinguish specific email rejection reasons (including the new `user.email.blocked` coming from `EmailValidator`/`BlockedEmail.should_block?`). However, the response already includes `message: ... user.errors.full_messages ...`, so “enumeration” is not uniquely enabled by the new fields; it’s more of an API/info-disclosure design concern than a clearly verifiable new security defect caused solely by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:11 — BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a DB write (counter update) during model validation on every signup attempt, adding write load and taking a row lock in the request path; consider debouncing or async stats updates

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmailValidator#validate_each` calling `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb), and `BlockedEmail.should_block?` does `record.match_count += 1`, sets `last_match_at`, and `record.save` when a row exists (app/models/blocked_email.rb). That means each validation hit on a blocked email performs a DB write/row update in the request path, which can add write load and contention. This is a real performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, not necessarily a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/models/blocked_email.rb:23 — self.action_type ||= BlockedEmail.actions[:block] relies on Enum not starting at 0; if :block maps to 0, ||= treats the explicitly-set value as unset (fragile if the enum changes)

adjudication.rationale: In Ruby, `||=` only overwrites when the left-hand side is `nil` or `false`. An enum value of `0` is truthy, so `self.action_type ||= BlockedEmail.actions[:block]` in `BlockedEmail#set_defaults` will NOT treat an explicitly-set `0` as unset. The claimed bug about `:block` mapping to 0 causing overwrite is therefore incorrect based on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] lib/validators/email_validator.rb — file is missing a trailing newline, which can cause patch/tooling churn

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly shows `\ No newline at end of file` for `lib/validators/email_validator.rb`, so the file does lack a trailing newline, but this is a formatting/tooling nit rather than a correctness defect or substantial review issue per the category definitions.
